$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the only stored verdict carrying a finding with a null file and
a null line, so it is the only case that pins what the scorer does with one. The CLI keeps such a
finding deliberately, because dropping it would leave the verdict documenting fewer findings than the
report and than its own summary line counted.
The scorer counts it in `unlocated` and nowhere else. It cannot match a plant, because matching needs
a line to compare. It is not a definite false positive, because those are findings against the clean
control and this one names no file. It is not unattributed either, because that is a finding on a
seeded fixture and this one names no fixture. Folding it into the rate's denominator would dilute the
false-positive share with a finding nobody can check, so `reported` is 9 while the verdict carries 10.
It scored null until scorer v2, for a reason that no longer exists: the old parser read adjacency in
the markdown, counted nine, compared that with the ten violations declared, and refused the run.
The report is CONSTRUCTED, from full-recall's report with a tenth block added. The shape is real:
test/fixtures/test-review-cli/reports/finding-without-location.md exists because a finding with a row
and no location is something reports actually contain.
derivation: The verdict declares 4 Critical, 4 High, 1 Medium and 1 Low, which sums to 10, and carries ten
findings. Nine name a file and a line: C1, C3, C4, C5, H1, H3, H4, H10 and L1, all at the lines their
rules fire on. The tenth cites Row M3 with file null and line null, because its block carries no
The tenth is filtered out before matching, so unlocated is 1 and reported is 9.
The nine that remain are full-recall's nine, at the same lines, so every plant matches: hits 9,
criticalHits 4 of 4, misses empty, falsePositives 0, unattributed 0.
The counts the harness derives from these: recall 9/9 = 1.00, CRITICAL recall 4/4 = 1.00,
nonFalsePositiveRate (9 - 0)/9 = 1.00. Counting the M3 in the denominator instead would give 10/10 =
1.00 here and would hide a real false positive on a run that had one, which is why it is counted
beside the rate rather than inside it.
The verdict's own numbers come from cli/lib/parse-report.js reading this report:
100 - 4x10 - 4x5 - 1x2 - 1x1 = 37, and any Critical at all forces Block. The M3 deducts two points
and contributes nothing to recall, which is the same split partially-attributed records.
No finding names a file outside the review set, so outOfScope is 0 and falsePositives is unchanged by it.
